facts.claim: South Gippsland, also called Prom Country after Wilsons Promontory, takes in the southernmost point of the Australian mainland.
Its attractions range from coastal parks, beaches and mountain rainforests to maritime and coal-mining heritage.
The main route is the South Gippsland Highway, turning off the Princes Highway at Dandenong; the Prom Country Information Centre at Korumburra is about a 90-minute drive from Melbourne.
Wonthaggi's State Coal Mine worked from 1910 to 1968 and is now run by Parks Victoria as a heritage area with a cafe.

The Grand Ridge Road is an unsealed road through remnant Strzelecki Ranges rainforest, called Gippsland's inland equivalent to the Great Ocean Road, with Tarra-Bulga National Park's suspension bridge walk on it.
The shire covers 3,296 sq km, had 30,577 people in 2021 and includes Leongatha (council seat), Korumburra, Foster and Meeniyan.

experiences: Walk wild coastal parks and beaches
Explore the State Coal Mine's mining heritage
Cycle the Great Southern Rail Trail

tips.title: Drive, don't rely on buses
tips.detail: V/Line's daily bus runs only from Melbourne to Yarram, so reaching the coastal parks and towns is realistic only by car.

tips.title: Stop at the info centre
tips.detail: The Prom Country Information Centre on the South Gippsland Highway at Korumburra is the region's main visitor centre, about 90 minutes from Melbourne.

best_months.rationale: Coast, beach and trail region; summer to early autumn suits beaches, the Bunurong coast and rail-trail riding. Inferred from Wikivoyage's coastal and outdoor focus, not an explicit best-time statement: UNVERIFIED.

facts.claim: Horsham is a regional city on a bend in the Wimmera River, about 300 km north-west of Melbourne, and the most populous city in the Wimmera (20,429 people in 2021).
Horsham is the gateway to the Silo Art Trail and the north-western side of the Grampians National Park.
Mount Arapiles, about 30 minutes' drive west, is one of Australia's premier rock-climbing sites, rising about 140 m above the plains; Parks Victoria charges a camping fee at its campground.
Horsham's town sights include the Horsham Regional Art Gallery, the Botanic Gardens and the riverside, and it is a popular stopover on the Western Highway, within about 4 hours' drive of Melbourne.
Natimuk, near Mount Arapiles, is an attractive town with old buildings and a wide main street.

tips.title: Bring water to Arapiles
tips.detail: Tank water at the Mount Arapiles campground is not for drinking, so bring your own and plenty of it.

tips.title: Summer heat
tips.detail: Horsham sees about 25 extreme-heat days a year and January averages a 30.6C maximum, so plan outdoor time for cooler months.

best_months.rationale: Summers are warm to hot and dry with frequent extreme heat, winters cool and misty (July max 13.6C); autumn and spring are the mild shoulder seasons. Months are an inference from the climate text.

facts.claim: The 31,000 ha park lies about 350 km north-east of Melbourne; its plateau reaches 1,723 m at The Horn, the park's highest point.
It was reserved on 4 November 1898, making it one of Australia's oldest national parks.
The plateau has striking granite boulders and rock formations, sheer cliffs, waterfalls and snow gum woodland.
The Mount Buffalo Chalet, built in 1910, overlooks large sheets of granite and has views of the Ovens and Buckland valleys; its cafe is open weekends and public holidays.
From December to March the plateau's grassy plains carry wildflowers; in winter Cresta Valley and Dingo Dell offer tobogganing, snow play and cross-country skiing.
Bogong moths shelter in the rock crevices at The Horn, and birds feed on them.

experiences: Walk granite tors and plateau lookouts
Camp among snow gums by Lake Catani
Toboggan and ski cross-country in winter

tips.title: Carry snow chains
tips.detail: Snow chains must be carried every day, for all vehicles including 4WDs, and fitted where road signs say so; penalties apply.

tips.title: Stay in Bright or Porepunkah
tips.detail: There is no accommodation at the Chalet; visitors stay in the nearby towns of Porepunkah and Bright.

tips.title: Winter snow play
tips.detail: Dingo Dell and Cresta Valley are the beginner-friendly tobogganing and snow-play areas, and back-country skiing carries avalanche and weather risks.

best_months.rationale: December to March: wildflowers on the plateau and animals returning from the foothills; winter (snow) is the second season.

seasonal_tags: winter snow season (tobogganing and cross-country skiing at Cresta Valley and Dingo Dell; exact months UNVERIFIED)

facts.claim: Mildura is a regional city on the Victorian bank of the Murray River with 35,652 people in 2021 (about 58,900 with surrounding towns), and the largest settlement in Sunraysia.
The area grows about 80% of Victoria's grapes and more than 70% of Australia's dried vine fruits, plus citrus, avocados and almonds.
George Chaffey founded the irrigation settlement in 1887 after Alfred Deakin visited California's irrigation areas.
At Lock 11, a man-made island with walking tracks, paddle steamers pass through the lock and weir; Apex Park has what is billed as Victoria's largest inland beach.
The Murray can be cruised on the Paddlesteamer Melbourne or a chartered houseboat, and Mungo National Park is about two hours away for a day trip.
Mildura is nearer Adelaide than Melbourne: 6-7 hours' drive from Melbourne, 4.5-5 from Adelaide, with flights from Melbourne and Sydney.

experiences: Taste Sunraysia wine and fresh produce
Swim and walk the river's sandbars

tips.title: Fruit fly zone
tips.detail: Mildura is in a fruit-fly-free zone: don't bring fruit or vegetables in from outside it, or take them out across the zone or interstate borders. Fines can reach $100,000.

tips.title: Hire a car
tips.detail: Most attractions need a car; local buses run on weekdays in business hours, and rental companies operate from the airport.

best_months.rationale: Summers are hot, with maxima averaging 32C and some days over 40C; winters average 15C with frost. Autumn and spring are mild. Months are an inference from the climate text.
